jobs.occupation: Senior Data Engineer – Build the Data Foundation for Greener Rail
jobs.description:
Cubris · A Hitachi Rail company · Ballerup, Denmark · On-site with flexibility

Would you like to use your expertise in Python, geospatial data and data platforms to make rail operations smarter and more energy-efficient? At Cubris, you will play a central role in developing the data foundation behind solutions that help train operators reduce energy consumption and improve punctuality.

We are looking for an experienced Senior Data Engineer who enjoys shaping technical direction, building solutions and working closely with colleagues across engineering, architecture and product.

Your role

You will help shape the data platform and geospatial model supporting our GreenSpeed® platform and Infrastructure Management System. You will turn complex railway data into a consistent, reliable foundation for our software – covering everything from tracks, signals and stations to gradients, speed limits and temporary restrictions.

Your main responsibilities will be to:

• 
Develop our data platform and geospatial model: Define schemas, feature classes, linear referencing using track and chainage, topology rules and railway asset attributes.

• 
Build robust Python data pipelines: Ingest, transform and integrate data, and automate workflows using Airflow or similar orchestration tools.

• 
Develop spatial storage and cloud solutions: Work with PostgreSQL/PostGIS or equivalent technologies, preferably on Microsoft Azure, and apply graph-based structures where they add value.

• 
Ensure data quality and traceability: Validate geometries, topology and attributes, and document data models and workflows with appropriate versioning and change control.

• 
Translate requirements into practical solutions: Collaborate with architects, software engineers, product managers and DevOps to deliver solutions that meet today’s needs and evolve with our products.

What you bring

You have substantial hands-on experience in data platform development and architecture, and you enjoy both making technical decisions and implementing them.

We are particularly interested in your:

• 
Strong Python skills and experience with scalable data pipelines, data integration and orchestration tools such as Airflow.

• 
Experience with GeoPandas, Shapely, GDAL/OGR, PyProj or equivalent geospatial technologies, including LineString and MultiLineString geometries.

• 
Knowledge of PostgreSQL/PostGIS or other spatial databases.

• 
Experience developing cloud-native data solutions, preferably on Microsoft Azure.

• 
Ability to work independently when requirements are evolving and documentation is still taking shape.

We also welcome a strong engineering grounding in industrial systems. You may have developed this through your education or through experience in transport, manufacturing, energy or automation. You understand how software, data and physical infrastructure interact, and how to translate real-world assets and operating conditions into accurate data models. You also appreciate the demands for quality, reliability and traceability in systems used in daily operations.

Experience with QGIS or ArcGIS, graph-based data structures and algorithms, safety-critical systems, railway technology or EBuLa integration would be an advantage.

As a colleague, you share your knowledge, contribute ideas and enjoy solving problems with others. You can balance long-term technical quality with practical delivery.

Why join Cubris?

You will have a real say in technical decisions and product development in a company where ideas can quickly become action. Our flat, agile organisation encourages open dialogue and gives you room to take ownership.

You will join a small, autonomous team backed by Hitachi Rail’s international expertise and resources. Your work will serve a clear purpose: smarter rail operations with lower energy consumption and CO₂ emissions.

The role is based in Ballerup, Denmark. We value close collaboration in the office while offering flexibility.

About Cubris

Cubris is a Danish software company and has been part of Hitachi Rail since 2024. Our award-winning GreenSpeed® platform helps train operators optimise driving, reduce energy consumption and improve punctuality. We develop technology for Driver Advisory Systems (DAS), Automatic Train Operation (ATO) and advanced data analytics.

Interested in joining us?

We would love to hear about your experience, your ideas and what motivates you. Send us your application and CV, or get in touch if you would like to learn more about the role and life at Cubris.

jobs.occupation: Full-time PhD position(s) on conspiracy theories in political communication at the Digital Democracy Centre  (5+3 or 4+4 scheme)
jobs.description:
Full-time PhD position(s) on conspiracy theories in political communication at the Digital Democracy Centre (5+3 or 4+4 scheme)

The Digital Democracy Centre (DDC) at the University of Southern Denmark, Odense, invites applications for one or more full-time PhD positions studying conspiracy theories in political communication as part of the German Research Foundation-funded research unit Beyond Crazy: Integrating Benefits into the Analysis of Conspiracy Beliefs.

The project examines how conspiracy theories are shared in political communication, how the media and the public respond to such content, and how politicians perceive conspiracy theories. The project combines qualitative and quantitative social science methods, including content analysis, interviews, and social scientific experiments.

We are looking for motivated candidates from communication, psychology, journalism, political science, sociology, or related disciplines who are interested in conducting high-quality research with societal relevance.

The position can be applied for under either the 5+3 or 4+4 PhD scheme. Employment is expected to start in April 2027 or soon thereafter, and the place of employment is Odense.

For full details about the position, eligibility requirements, PhD schemes and application process, please read the full job advertisement and apply via SDU's website.

Application deadline: 11th of December 2026, 11:59 PM/23:59 (CET/CEST)

**Student Analyst in Strategy & Transformation

**

**Who We Are

**

NNIT is a niche specialist in IT for life sciences and highly regulated industries. We help pharma, biotech and medtech companies across Europe, the US and Asia, as well as public sector and regulated customers in Denmark, solve their most complex challenges where technology, regulation and business critical processes meet.

We are in the middle of a fundamental transformation. Our strategy, OneNNIT 2030, sets out how we will sharpen our position as a niche specialist, reshape our portfolio into a focused set of value pathways that take customers from advisory through implementation to managed services, bring our US and European organisations together as one, and become a genuinely AI-driven company.

The Strategy & Transformation Office leads that journey. It reports directly to our CEO, owns NNIT's strategy cycle, runs the transformation programme and builds the capabilities that will carry the momentum through to 2030. We are now building the team, and we are looking for a Student Analyst who wants to work at the heart of it.

**What You Will Do

**

This is not a back-office student job. You will work on the same questions as our CEO and Executive Management, and you will see first-hand how strategy is set, decided and turned into action in a listed company.

You do not need to be a technical AI specialist. You should, however, care deeply about how AI reshapes organisations, ways of working and business models, because that question runs through everything we do.

**Typical tasks include

**

• Supporting the programme management of OneNNIT 2030, from planning and milestone tracking to following up on decisions across the organisation

• Preparing sharp decision material, presentations and updates for the CEO, Executive Management and the Board

• Analysing our offerings, markets and competitors as we shape the value pathways NNIT will take to market

• Supporting the annual strategy cycle and strategic projects, including the screening and assessment of partnerships and acquisitions

• Helping drive NNIT's journey to becoming an AI-driven company, across our offerings, our delivery model and our internal ways of working

• Contributing to the change management and internal communication that help colleagues understand and own the transformation

• Preparing and facilitating workshops and leadership meetings

**What You Will Bring

**

We imagine that you

• Are preferably in the third year of your Bachelor's degree, or in the first year of your Master’s degree, for example in Strategy, Organisation and Leadership at Copenhagen Business School

• Have a strong interest in strategy, transformation, change management and AI

• Are analytical and structured, and able to turn complex input into clear, well-argued recommendations

• Write well and build presentations that make their point quickly

• Have strong Excel and PowerPoint skills and are comfortable with the rest of Microsoft Office and everyday AI tools

• Communicate clearly and professionally in English, both written and spoken

• Take initiative, challenge your own thinking, handle confidential information with discretion and enjoy working with senior stakeholders

**What We Offer

**

You will join the Strategy & Transformation Office, which reports directly to the CEO, and work closely with the Head of Strategy & Transformation. You will have a front-row seat as NNIT redefines its strategy, organisation and portfolio, and you will work alongside Executive Management, senior leaders across Europe, the US and Asia, and our external advisors.

You will get real responsibility from day one, high exposure to senior leadership and the flexibility to balance work with your studies. Few student jobs offer a closer view of how strategy and transformation are done in practice.

**Practical Information

**

The role is 15 to 20 hours per week, with flexibility around exams.

Please upload your CV and cover letter in English. We review applications on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to apply soon.

About NNIT

NNIT is a publicly listed company that specializes in IT solutions to life sciences internationally, and to the public and enterprise sectors in Denmark. We focus on high complexity industries and thrive in environments where regulatory demands and complexity are high. We advise on and build sustainable digital solutions that work for the patients, citizens, employees, end users or customers.

NNIT consists of group company NNIT A/S and subsidiaries SCALES, Excellis Health Solutions and SL Controls. Together, these companies employ more than 1,600 people in Europe, Asia, and USA.

We celebrate diversity and are dedicated to fostering an inclusive environment for all employees. We actively work to eliminate bias and ensure an inclusive workplace where everyone has the right to be seen and heard as they are. We invite interested candidates to apply, no matter their background.

In the interest of fostering a fair and unbiased recruitment process, we kindly request candidates to refrain from including their pictures in their applications.

The Tech Collective, Data & AI

What you'll do

In this role, you’ll take client ideas from a rough hypothesis to a working prototype, and then to a production system that runs reliably. You'll design the architecture, write the code across frontend, backend, and data, and decide what to build and what to leave out. It's a hands-on role. Most of your time goes into building, and the rest goes into working with clients to make sure you’re building the right thing.

The work covers generative AI applications and agents, including the harnesses that make them reliable (tools, context, memory, orchestration, and guardrails), along with retrieval pipelines and the data flows they depend on. You’ll connect these to client systems, deploy them in the cloud, and set up the evals and observability you need to see whether they work and how to improve them. You’ll work closely with our data platform and AI specialists, review code, and help less experienced engineers grow.

What you'll bring

You're a builder at heart. You have a master's degree in computer science, engineering, or a related field, (preferably) 5+ years of hands-on software experience, and a track record of shipping production-ready software systems. Ideally, you also have experience with the whole software development lifecycle: starting with an idea (whether your own or a stakeholder’s), designing the solution architecture, developing and testing the solution, and putting it into the hands of actual users. Good engineering matters to you, but you’re not a purist, you care more about shipping something that works and solves the problem.

What sets you apart is depth beyond the code. You know AI (LLMs, agents, RAG, evals) and data (data modelling, pipelines, event-driven, and real-time systems) well enough that others come to you for it. Ideally, you know a bit of both.

You're equally at home building AI products and building with AI. Coding agents and AI-assisted tools are part of how you work every day, and you use them critically. You know where they make you faster and where the output needs a careful human eye.

To be a great fit, it helps if you have:

• 
Solid full-stack skills in Python and/or TypeScript (e.g., React, Next.js, FastAPI), with production systems to show for it

• 
Hands-on experience building agents and the harnesses around them (tool use, MCP, context and memory management, orchestration, guardrails), and designing the data models and pipelines that real products run on

• 
An AI-native way of working, using coding agents such as Claude Code, Cursor, or Codex in your own development workflow, with a clear view of where they help and where they don’t

• 
Experience deploying and running solutions on AWS, Azure, or GCP, including containers, CI/CD, and enough observability to know what's going on

• 
System-level judgement: you can reason about architecture, trade-offs, and failure modes, and you can spot the weak points in an existing stack

• 
Curiosity about the client’s problem, and the ability to explain technical choices clearly to people who don’t write code

• 
A habit of helping others get better through sparring, pairing, and code reviews

English is our corporate language. Proficiency in one or more additional languages is a plus.

What we offer

At The Tech Collective, you’ll join a team of 30 consultants that feels closer to a nerdy startup than a large consultancy, while being firmly backed by Implement Consulting Group. You’ll own what you build, and you’ll have the freedom to shape your role in the direction that motivates you.

You’ll work on data and AI problems across industries, alongside experienced peers in AI, data, and software. Our culture is built on trust, curiosity, humility, and impact, with high autonomy, co-creation, and active knowledge-sharing.

Ready to build with us? We review applications on an ongoing basis, so apply as soon as you can.

jobs.occupation: Senior Store Operation & Retail Delivery Manager
jobs.description:
Are you passionate about driving operational excellence, improving business performance, and enabling retail teams to deliver outstanding results? Then we might have just the job for you at Specsavers.

Join Specsavers as our new Senior Store Operations & Retail Delivery Manager and play a key role in shaping operational performance, supporting retail transformation initiatives, and driving sustainable growth across Northern Europe.

Your role

As our Senior Store Operations & Retail Delivery Manager, you will be responsible for supporting the execution of strategic initiatives, operational plans, and performance improvement programmes across our Northern Europe retail business.

Working closely with the Director of Stores, Heads of Stores, Business Performance Managers, and Regional Relationship Managers, you will help create the conditions for stores to improve profitability, strengthen operational excellence, and deliver outstanding customer experiences.

You will act as a key link between regional field teams, support functions, and business leaders, ensuring that the right tools, frameworks, and initiatives are in place to support long-term business success. You are a strong collaborator who thrives in complex environments, enjoys working across functions, and is motivated by helping others achieve measurable business results.

Finally, you are ready an everyday where you combine working from home with being at the Northern European Support Office in Copenhagen along with frequent visits to the countries in the region.

Key responsibilities include:

• Driving business improvement and performance programmes across multiple markets.

• Identifying opportunities to improve profitability, efficiency, and operational performance.

• Supporting strategic planning and execution together with regional and country stakeholders.

• Ensuring retail tools, processes, and initiatives are effectively implemented and continuously improved.

• Building strong partnerships across functions to deliver sustainable business outcomes.

Your new team

You'll join the Northern Europe Store Operations function and work closely with senior retail leaders, business performance specialists, regional relationship managers, and a broad range of support functions.

The team plays an important role in supporting our store network, helping country teams deliver sustainable growth, operational excellence, and outstanding customer experiences.

As part of an international and highly collaborative environment, you'll contribute to projects and initiatives that directly influence business performance across multiple markets.

What are we looking for?

We are preferably looking for a candidate with the following competencies:

• Strong experience in retail operations, business performance, or operational excellence.

• Experience from a similar role or i.e. a Regional Relationship Manager role

• Commercial and financial acumen, including business planning and performance analysis.

• Experience leading cross-functional projects and driving measurable business improvements.

• Working with operating and supporting teams individually and remotely

• Excellent stakeholder management, communication, and influencing skills.

• A data-driven and analytical approach to solving business challenges.

It would be an advantage if you have:

• Leadership experience working in franchise, partnership, or multi-site retail environments.

• Experience across multiple markets or countries.

• Knowledge of business transformation, change management, or performance improvement programmes.

• Experience using Power BI or similar reporting tools.

As a person, we believe that you are:

• Commercially minded and focused on creating results.

• A strong collaborator who builds trust and alignment across teams.

• Structured, proactive, and comfortable managing complexity.

• An engaging communicator who can influence stakeholders at all levels.

What awaits you upon joining Specsavers

At Specsavers, you'll get more than just a job. You will join us on a journey to make eye health and hearing services accessible to everyone.

We offer an exciting and challenging role in an organisation with strong ambitions, where you'll be part of a collaborative and supportive culture.

Joining us, you’ll get:

• Competitive compensation and benefits.

• Professional and personal development opportunities.

• A collaborative and inclusive culture.

• The opportunity to influence business performance across multiple countries.

• Exposure to senior stakeholders and strategic initiatives within an international organisation.

Is this your next step? Then apply today

To apply, please send us your CV using the button below. We want to respect your time, so including an application letter is optional. Feel free to apply as soon as possible. Please avoid including any photos or references to your age in your CV. It contributes to a fairer and more unbiased assessment.

We review CVs and invite candidates for interviews on an ongoing basis. Our recruitment process typically consists of an initial screening, two rounds of interviews, and a personality assessment feedback session.

If you have any questions regarding the role, please contact the hiring manager Jacob Vejen by e-mail: jacob.vejen@specsavers.com.

Diversity & Inclusion at Specsavers

Specsavers will consider all qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, colour, religion, sex, age, national origin, disability, veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity, or any other legally protected factor.

In line with our commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion, we integrate these principles into all aspects of our work, from product development to team building.

jobs.occupation: Legal Counsel - Employment Law Leaning (Mat Cover)
jobs.description:
About Pleo

Messy spend management is tricky business. And tedious processes are a lose-lose situation for all involved, not just finance. At Pleo, we're changing that. We build spend solutions that make managing money seamless, empowering, and surprisingly effective for finance teams and employees alike - with a vision to help all businesses ‘go beyond’.

The word ‘Pleo’ actually means ‘more than you’d expect’, and living by that mantra has been the secret to our success over the last 10 years.

Now, we’re at a pivotal moment in our journey; every move we make has a direct impact on our 40,000+ customers, our business, and our collective success. We need people who take pride in uncovering customer needs, who turn complex problems into simple solutions, challenge the way things are done (respectfully), and always aim high. With great ambitions driving us forward, we can’t say we’ve got this whole thing figured out. And frankly, that’s half the fun! What we can say is that we’re a driven, progressive, and, importantly, a kind bunch of 850+ people from over 100 nationalities, all committed to delivering the future of business spending, together.

About the role

We're looking for an interim In-house Legal Counsel to join our Legal team at Pleo in Copenhagen, Denmark. In this role, you'll serve as a trusted legal advisor across the business, protecting our interests and enabling growth as we scale our fintech platform. If you're excited about working at the intersection of legal strategy and operational excellence, and are passionate about building a compliant, well-governed fintech company, then this is the opportunity for you!

Please note that the role is a parental leave cover and therefore fixed-term until 30 September 2027.

Who you’ll be working with and reporting to

You'll report to one of our Associate Director, Legal and work closely with teams in People, Fraud, Finance, Product, Compliance and Operations. Our legal team is highly collaborative and dedicated to managing legal risk while enabling business velocity.

What you’ll be doing

As an In-house Legal Counsel, you will:

• 
Serve as the primary point of contact for business queries across all departments, providing timely, practical legal guidance on day-to-day operational matters.

• 
Support our People team on employment law, workplace policies, and labor compliance, including contract reviews, policy drafting, and regulatory adherence across multiple jurisdictions.

• 
Corporate administration by drafting, reviewing, and amending internal policies, procedures, and standardised legal templates that the business can use efficiently.

• 
Assist managing fraud and compliance escalations by conducting liability assessments, performing compliance checks, and providing risk mitigation advice to protect the business.

• 
Assist with customer disputes and regulatory engagement with the UK Financial Ombudsman Service (FOS), supporting escalations, preparing responses, and helping to ensure we meet all regulatory deadlines and requirements.

What you bring

You'll thrive in this role if you have:

• 
A Cand.Jur or equivalent legal qualification recognised in Denmark.

• 
2-5 years of legal experience – ideally in fintech, financial services, or a fast-growing scale-up environment where you've handled a broad range of matters.

• 
Knowledge about employment law and HR compliance – you understand the nuances of employment contracts, workplace policies, and labor law across multiple jurisdictions.

• 
Strong vendor and contract management skills – you can review, negotiate, and draft commercial agreements efficiently.

• 
Excellent communication skills – you can translate complex legal concepts into practical business advice for non-legal stakeholders.

• 
A proactive, solutions-oriented mindset – you see problems as opportunities and can manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.

• 
Experience with compliance and risk management in a regulated industry is a plus as well as managing regulatory escalations and disputes, particularly with financial regulators or ombudsman services.

Why is this role a good fit for you

This role is a good fit for you if:

• 
You want a real look at how the law works in practice, where you implement it and explain it rather than argue it in theory

• 
You want genuine input into decisions, balancing the technically correct answer against what actually works commercially

• 
You like building things that outlast you: templates, policies and process that the business will use long after your contract ends

This role is not a good fit for you if:

• 
You want a clean roadmap. The team is under-resourced and the workload is heavy, so expect more firefighting than planned work

• 
You're looking for a permanent role. This is a 12-month fixed-term contract covering parental leave

• 
You want to specialise deeply or lead. This is a broad, hands-on individual contributor role where you'll be supported, not managing

How you’ll develop in this role

In your first three months at Pleo, you'll:

• 
Take over the routine employment workload so it runs independently of your manager

• 
Get to know the business well enough that your advice fits how Pleo actually operates, not just what the regulation says

• 
Start shaping the policies and templates the move from startup to corporate needs

Across the 12 months you'll build in-house practice and a working knowledge of fintech regulation that's hard to get anywhere else, with direct support from an experienced lead. Plenty of people use a contract like this as the step that takes them from theory into commercial legal work for good.

The location

This role will is a hybrid role with an expectation of spending on average 3 days a week in our Copenhagen office.

Show me the benefits!

💳 Your own Pleo card (no more out-of-pocket spending!)

🍜 Lunch is on us for your work days - enjoy catered meals or receive a lunch allowance based on your local office

🏥 Comprehensive private healthcare - depending on your location, coverage options include Vitality, Alan or Médis

🌴 We offer 25 days of holiday + your public holidays

🏠 For our Team, we offer both hybrid and fully remote working options

🏖️ Option to purchase 5 additional days of holiday through a salary sacrifice

❤️🩹 We use MyndUp to give our employees access to free mental health and well-being support with great success so far

👶 Paid parental leave - we want to make sure that we're supportive of families and help you feel that you don't have to compromise your family due to work

The interview process

We want to ensure you're set up for success and understand what will be expected of you. If your application is successful, our interview process is as follows:

• 
Intro call (30 minutes) – A chat with our Talent Partner to discuss the role, your background, and what's important to you in your next move.

• 
Interview with our Associate Director, Legal (45 minutes) – Meet to discuss how you see your role supporting the business, your approach to compliance culture, and your vision for the legal function.

• 
Final round with our Associate Director and General Counsel (60 minutes) – We'll dive deeper into your legal experience, explore specific scenarios you've handled, and discuss how you approach problem-solving in an in-house environment.

Transparency is important to us so we also wanted to share some insights about what we’re looking for in applications to ensure you can set yourself up for success!

Last time we hired a Legal Counsel, we received a large number of applications but only a finite number could be selected for an intro call. Some of the key reasons why previous candidates didn’t make it past the application screening stage include:

• 
CV writing and content: we receive a lot of CVs, and many of them are AI-generated. We love seeing people leverage AI (it’s a big focus for us internally too)but without human intervention, these CVs can sometimes become generic and fail to show a candidate in the best light. What we're really looking for is the specific details of real impact that only you know from your previous experience. A top tip from us is to use the “Achieved X, as measured by Y, by doing Z” formula (credit: Laszlo Bock, ~2014) to give a really clear picture of what you’ve worked on. A final note: including links to your previous companies' websites is a huge help and allows us to truly understand your background!

• 
Application care: every single application we receive is reviewed by a human (yes, hundreds of them) because we believe that candidates' efforts should be matched by an equal level of human care. This means that we expect a similar level of attention put into your application. Read and answer the application questions carefully, they make a huge difference in our decision-making process.

• 
Profile to role fit: highlight most important aspects of the role, points that might get misunderstood, any specific industry requirements etc.

About your application

• 
English first. Since it's our company language, please submit your application in English. You’ll be using it a lot if you join us.

• 
A fair look for everyone. Our talent team reads every single application to ensure the process is fair. To keep things running smoothly, we only accept applications through our system—our support team can’t pass on calls or emails.

• 
Diversity drives us. We can only reach our goals if our team reflects the world around us. That starts with you hitting apply, even if you don't tick every single box. We encourage people from all backgrounds and experiences to join us.

• 
Interview at your best. We want you to feel comfortable throughout the process. If you have any accessibility requirements or need a specific format, email belonging@pleo.io. We’ll design a process that works for you.

• 
Your data is safe. When you apply, we process your personal data as a data processor. For more information on how Pleo processes personal data, read our Privacy Policy here.

• 
Applying for multiple roles? Nothing is stopping you, and we assess every role independently. However, we do look for alignment, so make sure you can explain why your interest and experience are right for each specific role.

• 
Reapplying. If you’re applying for the same role again, please wait six months from your last decision before hitting submit.

Benefits to support your best work

Our benefits package is curated to support you fully, inside and outside of work.

Purchaser at Sekura Cabins in Randers

Have you gained some initial experience in purchasing and are you ready to develop your skills further?

At Sekura Cabins, we are looking for a Purchaser to join our Supply Chain team. You will work closely with suppliers, production and colleagues across the organization, taking responsibility for your own suppliers and tasks while learning from experienced colleagues.

You do not need many years of experience. What matters most is that you have a solid foundation in purchasing or supply chain, are curious, take responsibility and are keen to develop.

About the role

You will join our Supply Chain team of four Senior Purchasers and Purchasers in total, reporting to our Senior Manager, SCM.

Your primary focus will be operational purchasing and day-to-day contact with our suppliers. A key part of the role is following up on deliveries and ensuring that the right materials are available on time so that production can run as planned.

You will also work with selected suppliers and categories, with opportunities to prepare for and participate in negotiations. You will cooperate with our freight forwarders and become a key partner to colleagues across the organization.

The role is varied, and some days are fast-paced. It is therefore important that you can stay organized, see tasks through to completion and remain calm when several things need your attention at the same time.

Your responsibilities will include:

·       Maintaining daily contact with suppliers and following up with them

·       Processing purchase proposals and issuing purchase orders

·       Following up on order confirmations, lead time and deadlines

·       Checking prices and invoices

·       Coordinating and planning material supplies for production

·       Optimizing inventory levels based on forecasts

·       Booking collections and coordinating with our freight forwarders

·       Collaborating and following up across the organization

·       Updating and maintaining master data in our ERP system

About you

We imagine that you have some experience in purchasing, materials planning or supply chain and are now ready to take the next step and develop further.

You may also have a relevant qualification in, for example, Supply Chain Management, purchasing or logistics, combined with practical experience.

You are organized and detail-oriented, with strong communication and relationship-building skills. You enjoy working with a wide range of people and are comfortable picking up the phone, following up and making things happen.

We also value the following:

·       Good communication skills in Danish and English, both spoken and written

·       Knowledge of German is an advantage

·       Confidence using Microsoft 365, particularly Excel

·       Experience with Dynamics 365 Business Central is an advantage

·       Taking ownership of your tasks and seeing them through to completion

What we offer

At Sekura Cabins, you will have the opportunity to develop your skills in purchasing and supply chain in an international manufacturing company where decisions are quickly put into action.

You can look forward to:

·       Thorough training and ongoing support from experienced colleagues

·       Opportunities for professional development and greater responsibility as your skills grow

·       A role involving contact with a wide range of people

·       A canteen scheme

·       Health insurance

·       Dental insurance after three months of employment

We review applications and hold interviews on an ongoing basis and will fill the position once we have found the right candidate.

Please send your application and CV to HR Business Partner Camilla Scharling Markussen at csm@sekura.dk

If you have any questions about the role, please contact Steen Krogh on 87100550.

Spirii has spent the past seven years building the infrastructure behind EV charging in Europe. Today, we operate across multiple markets and support CPOs, fleets, workplaces, and public charging networks with software and hardware solutions that make EV charging simpler to manage and scale. We are headquartered in Copenhagen and part of the Edenred group.

We are now at an important stage of growth. The market is moving fast, our product is maturing, and our organisation is scaling. That brings new opportunities, new complexity, and a need for even stronger alignment and execution across the company.

The role

As Director of Strategy & Execution, you will be the operational centre of gravity for the Spirii leadership team. This is a high-impact role for someone who can hold strategic context, drive cross-functional execution, and step into whatever the moment requires.

In practice, that means moving between the strategic and the operational with ease. One week you may be preparing a board presentation or supporting a key business decision. The next, you are driving alignment across product and commercial, or bringing structure to an initiative that spans multiple teams. The role requires both breadth and depth — and the judgement to know which is needed.

What you will do

Strategic execution

• Work directly with the CEO and leadership team on the company’s most important priorities, translating direction into plans, and plans into measurable outcomes

• Drive the quarterly planning cycle, OKRs, and cross-functional initiatives from kickoff through to follow-through

• Support leadership decision-making by structuring information, surfacing trade-offs, and ensuring the right inputs are in place

Leadership alignment

• Own the operating rhythm of the leadership team — weekly syncs, planning sessions, offsites, and follow-up

• Identify where alignment is breaking down across commercial, product, engineering, and operations — and address it proactively

• Serve as a trusted connector across the organisation, helping teams stay coordinated and focused on shared priorities

Special projects

• Lead high-impact projects that do not naturally sit within one department, and work with Edenred stakeholders on shared initiatives and reporting when needed

• Take complex, ambiguous problems, define them clearly, and drive them through to resolution

Communication

• Support the CEO in communicating clearly across the organisation — all-hands updates, leadership messaging, and internal communications during periods of change

• Prepare board materials, investor presentations, and executive reviews

What we’re looking for

• 4–8 years of experience in a corporate development, management consulting, strategy, or general management role — ideally with exposure to B2B software

• Comfortable operating in ambiguity: you build the structure rather than waiting for it

• Strong written communication — you can turn a messy situation into a one-pager

• Commercially literate enough to sit in a room with customers or partners and follow the conversation

• Fluency in English required; Danish and/or German a plus given our footprint

• Discretion. You’ll see confidential commercial, board, and people matters — trust has to be earned fast and kept

• Genuine curiosity about EV charging, energy, or infrastructure software is a plus, not a requirement — but you’ll need to get fluent in OCPP, ISO 15118, and how CPMS/eMSP actually make money, quickly

Benefits

It is important for us to create a healthy, diverse, fun, and creative working environment, so besides all the basic benefits, we also focus a lot on social activities, flexible working hours and a good work-life balance.

• Flexible Work Environment: Enjoy a collaborative, inclusive, and open workplace designed to fit your needs and support work-life balance.

• Competitive Package: A competitive salary, an 11% company pension plan, and a comprehensive benefits package.

• Time to Recharge: Benefit from 32 paid vacation days and paid parental leave to focus on what matters most.

• Career Growth: Access professional development opportunities and grow your career in a high-impact, high-growth industry.

• Stay Energized: Enjoy excellent coffee, tea, free snacks, and subsidized lunches at the office.

• Stay Active: Use our Spirii gym and shared company car to keep moving.

• Make an Impact: Be part of a team driving the future of sustainable energy while working on meaningful projects.

The position is a permanent position in Copenhagen, Denmark. Danish language is not a requirement, but fluent English language skills are required.

About Spirii – Who We Are

Spirii is a full-service e-mobility provider which offers hardware and software charging solutions to companies in the private and the public sector. Spirii was founded seven years ago as a company. Nevertheless, the people in Spirii have extensive experience working with electric cars and charging, as well as the development of future transport- and energy systems.

Spirii is an equal opportunity employer. We encourage applications from candidates of all backgrounds and experiences. Spirii strives to create an inclusive and diverse workplace, and we encourage all qualified applicants to apply regardless of age, gender, race, sexual/religious orientation, or disability.

Job Title: Data Governance Professional, Privacy and AI Compliance

Department: Enterprise IT & Quality

Location: Greater Copenhagen Area/ Ballerup /Denmark

As a Data Governance Professional, you will help shape how Novo and Enterprise IT put privacy and AI compliance requirements into practice. You will combine policy development with hands-on operational support, working across data governance with a strong focus on privacy, the responsible use of AI and data science, and their links to information security.

You will take ownership of maintaining and developing privacy requirements, controls and supporting guidance for IT solutions. Working directly with IT teams and data owners, you will help translate these requirements into workable solutions and carry improvements through to implementation. As Lead Data Ethics Responsible (DER) for Enterprise IT, you will also coordinate local privacy and AI compliance activities and drive our DER network.

You will work alongside experienced colleagues who provide professional guidance and specialist support. You will bring curiosity about technology, analytical thinking and the drive to move work forward, taking increasing responsibility and working more independently as your expertise grows.

Your new role

Your key responsibilities will include:

• Maintaining and developing privacy requirements, controls and guidance for IT solutions, translating regulatory and internal requirements into practical expectations across the IT and data lifecycle.

• Working with relevant specialists and process owners to keep this content current, address gaps and agree changes through the relevant governance processes.

• Providing practical support to IT teams and data owners on privacy and AI compliance, including documenting processing activities, supporting risk and impact assessments, and following up on agreed actions.

• Acting as Lead DER for Enterprise IT, driving and maintaining our local DER network, coordinating shared activities and helping colleagues carry out their responsibilities.

• Contributing to policies and frameworks covering privacy, AI and data science, and information security, in collaboration with stakeholders across Novo.

• Helping shape and deliver projects that improve how we manage, use and protect data, including simplifying compliance processes and supporting implementation of requirements and controls.

• Developing and delivering guidance, training and communication that make requirements easier to understand and apply.

You will have a defined area of responsibility, with specialist support and clear routes for decisions and escalation on complex matters.

Your new department

IT Process & Compliance defines, governs and continuously improves fit-for-purpose IT and data processes. We help the organisation meet regulatory expectations and provide insight and practical partnering to strengthen compliance across Novo.

Our work covers process management, compliance awareness and partnering, and support for audits and inspections. We also drive the privacy agenda across Enterprise IT, helping the organisation protect personal information and meet data protection requirements.

We work closely with stakeholders across Novo to turn requirements and identified issues into practical improvements. You will join colleagues with different professional backgrounds who work together across policy development, operational compliance and project delivery.

Your skills & qualifications

You are at the beginning of your career and want to develop at the intersection of governance, compliance and technology. You may be a recent graduate or have some relevant experience from employment, a student position, an internship or project work.

We are looking for someone who brings:

• A relevant degree, for example in law, IT, digital governance, data science or business, or equivalent relevant experience.

• A foundation or interest in privacy and data protection, gained through study or practical experience, and an interest in AI governance, data governance and information security.

• Curiosity about how IT solutions, AI and data science work, including how data is collected, used, shared and retained.

• An analytical approach and the ability to translate complex information into clear explanations and practical actions.

• Good collaboration skills and the confidence to ask questions, seek input and follow up with stakeholders.

• Fluency in written and spoken English.

You enjoy both analysing a problem and completing the work needed to solve it. You organise your tasks, take responsibility for agreed deliverables and recognise when specialist input is needed. You look for ways to make compliance simpler and more effective.

We do not expect you to be a specialist in every area. We expect you to bring a relevant foundation, sound judgement and a willingness to learn.

Working at Novo Nordisk

Every day we seek the solutions that defeat serious chronic diseases. To do this, we approach our work with determination, constant curiosity and a commitment to finding better ways forward. For over 100 years, this dedication has driven us to build a company focused on lasting change for long-term health. One where diverse thinking, shared purpose and mutual respect come together to create extraordinary results. As we continue our digital transformation journey, you'll find exciting opportunities to grow your expertise while working alongside talented colleagues who share your passion for excellence. When you join us, you're not just optimizing processes – you're enabling innovations that span generations.

What we offer

At Novo Nordisk, you’ll join a global healthcare company with a unique culture and strong results. We offer continuous learning, career development, and benefits tailored to your life and career stage.

Your impact begins here

As Consumer Analytics & Reporting Lead, you will be responsible for turning large, complex consumer data into dashboards, reports and analysis that Consumer Care and regional teams can trust and act on. You will build the reporting engine behind consumer campaigns across digital media, NovoCare, WegovyCare and other DtP channels, with consistent KPIs and validated data. Your work helps teams see what drives results, optimise faster and engage people living with serious chronic diseases in more relevant ways.

What you’ll bring

• A Bachelor’s degree in analytics, statistics, marketing, business or a related discipline; equivalent relevant experience may be considered.

• Relevant experience in consumer or marketing analytics.

• Experience delivering technical projects, including estimating development, managing dependencies, reviewing deliverables, and driving rollout and adoption.

• Experience with recurring performance reporting across diverse data sources.

• The ability to assess data quality and measurement limitations, distinguish correlation from causation and turn findings into testable recommendations.

• Good change management skills, including driving adoption of new tools, workflows and capabilities across diverse teams.

• An understanding of privacy, consent and promotional review considerations when using consumer engagement data.

• A structured, curious and commercially minded approach, with the ability to explain evidence, uncertainty and actions in plain language.

• A collaborative, influential and organised way of working, balancing recurring reporting with deeper analysis and following through on agreed actions.

Useful, but not essential:

• Intermediate Power BI development experience, including basic DAX, Power Query, SQL and data modelling.

• Experience in FMCG.

• Experience with brand tracking and social listening.

What you’ll do

You will be the hands-on link between consumer strategy and the data that shows whether it is working. For some projects you will build and model the data yourself; for others you will lead the collaboration with platform teams to get the right data in place.

• Partner with Consumer Care and regional teams to understand what success looks like for consumer engagement, and turn it into practical analytics and reporting.

• Build, maintain and improve consumer analytics solutions, such as dashboards or agents, and act as the Consumer Care super user.

• Establish a reliable reporting engine with unified KPI and metric definitions, clean and documented data, and recurring business reports covering journeys and campaigns across digital media, NovoCare, WegovyCare, partner sites and other DtP channels.

• Agree campaign objectives, KPIs, benchmarks and reporting cadence with campaign owners at activation, and specify data, tagging and tracking requirements with platform and data owners.

• Validate results, investigate discrepancies, troubleshoot issues and manage access, so reports truthfully display results.

• Track brand health and social conversation, assess what drives results across audiences, messages and touchpoints, and lead insight review sessions that turn findings into campaign optimisation and prioritised actions.

Who you’ll work with

You will join Consumer Care, Content & Media in Product & Portfolio Strategy, reporting to Alejandra Betancourt. In Product & Portfolio Strategy, colleagues work across markets to serve people around the world and help improve health at scale.

Your closest partners will be the Consumer Care team and global and regional consumer teams, who you will help turn strategy into measurement plans and reporting. You will also work with Enterprise AI, platform and data owners, and the teams responsible for our CDP data foundation to enable data access, pipelines and tracking. Stakeholder feedback will help shape the priorities and roadmap of the Content & Media team.

Your scope is global, primarily excluding the US and China, with reporting and insight support for relevant regions and affiliates. You will adapt analyses to local channel availability, market context and applicable requirements, always in alignment with regional representatives.

What you can expect here

You will work in an international environment where your expertise is valued and your voice is heard. You will be trusted to take ownership of the quality and reliability of consumer analytics, supported by colleagues across Consumer Care, regional teams, Enterprise AI and platform teams. Working across functions and markets gives you the opportunity to build new skills, broaden your perspective and see your work adopted by teams who rely on it.
